name: Advanced Sheet Metal
old_description: Precision-fabricated sheet metal products for residential and commercial roofing systems across Arizona.
about:
Advanced Sheet Metal, a family-owned metal fabrication company, was founded in 2006 in Phoenix, Arizona. The business operates manufacturing facilities in both Phoenix and Tucson, serving the Arizona market with precision-fabricated sheet metal components for roofing systems.

The company specializes in standing seam metal roofing panels, custom flashing, coping, trim, soffit systems, and a full range of roofing accessories. Every item is made to specification with flexible options for profiles, colors, gauges, and finishes. Fabrication is performed in-house at its two Arizona plants, though the company does not disclose headcount or annual volume.

Advanced Sheet Metal supplies residential and commercial roofing contractors and builders across Arizona. Its product line is tailored for roofing systems used in both new construction and retrofit projects, with an emphasis on quick turnaround for job-site delivery.

The company emphasizes fast, efficient turnaround times, stating that most orders are fabricated and shipped faster than the industry average without cutting corners. Its family-owned, Arizona-focused structure is presented as a differentiator, allowing direct control over quality and scheduling.

name: Advanced Technology of Kentucky
old_description: Founded in 1990, Advanced Technology of Kentucky, also known as Advanced Technologies, and now as ATI MEDICAL SUPPLIES, has been working to provide patients with braces, mobility aids, cold therapy products, respiratory aids, and a number of other DME items to help them recover from a disease, recent injury or surgery.
about:
Advanced Technology of Kentucky, now operating as ATI Medical Supplies, was founded in 1990 in Florence, Kentucky. The company began as Advanced Technologies before adopting its current name, focusing on supplying durable medical equipment and clinical supplies to healthcare providers across the region.

The firm distributes a broad range of DME products including orthopedic bracing for neck, spine, shoulder, arm, wrist, hip, knee, foot, and ankle; cold therapy and continuous passive motion devices; bone stimulation and splinting systems; mobility aids such as crutches, walkers, canes, and bathroom safety equipment; lymphedema pumps and sleeves; respiratory devices including CPAP, nebulizers, and pulse oximeters; electrotherapy units for pain management; and hospital beds, wheelchairs, and incontinence supplies. In addition to product distribution, ATI operates an outside billing service that handles insurance claims for manufacturers and sales representatives bringing new products to market.

Customers include hospitals, surgery centers, urgent care clinics, orthopedic and primary care physician offices, home health agencies, rehabilitation centers, and college and high school athletic clinics throughout Ohio and Kentucky. The billing service extends to manufacturers and marketing teams nationwide seeking reimbursement support for DME products.

The company states its mission is to provide the highest quality medical supplies so healthcare providers can quickly treat patients and improve quality of life. It aims to simplify the insurance process, offering direct payment options when coverage is unavailable, and maintains contracts covering 99 percent of plans in Ohio and Kentucky including Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurers, and workers' compensation, with additional Medicare and commercial contracts nationwide.

about:
Affordable Conveyor Services LLC is based in Southington, Connecticut. Founded in 2006, the company is owned and managed by Philip J. Robotham Jr., who brings over 30 years of experience in conveyor installation, repair, and maintenance. The business was built on a combined 60 years of industry experience among its team.

The firm provides end-to-end conveyor system services nationwide, including installation, preventive maintenance, emergency and routine repairs, safety inspections, system audits, replacements, upgrades, relocations, and alterations. It also services specialty equipment such as vertical reciprocating conveyors, stretch-wrap and band-strapping machines, mezzanines, racking, cranes, hoists, monorails, baggage handling systems, and pharmaceutical- and food-grade conveyors. Additional capabilities encompass site supervision, project management, controls and electrical repairs, pneumatic piping, and system modifications. The company operates with a small team of licensed technicians and offers 24/7 emergency response.

Its customers span distribution centers, retail fulfillment and warehousing operations, packaging and shipping centers, pharmaceutical manufacturing plants, airports and baggage handling facilities, and food and beverage processing facilities.

The company emphasizes competitiveness and attention to quality workmanship that exceeds customer expectations, with a focus on cost-effective solutions and immediate service availability.

name: Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance
old_description: Since 1978, we have been supplying our customers with not only the auto parts they seek, but a level of customer service and commitment unmatched. And you don’t have to be an auto dealer or auto repair facility to buy the auto parts you need. Stop by and see us and one of our friendly Parts Specialists will help you out.
about:
Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance is headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, and traces its origins to 1978. The organization operates as a cooperative network of independent warehouse distributors rather than a single-owner enterprise; no individual founders are named in public materials. It began as a program to supply auto parts and service support to independent businesses across North America and has since expanded its footprint to include Mexico, Honduras, Colombia, Belize, Europe, and China.

The alliance manages two consumer-facing brands — Auto Value and Bumper to Bumper — under which thousands of parts stores and certified service centers operate. Its core services include warehouse distribution, private-label parts branding (Perfect Stop, Parts Master, Perfect View, MacPherson, Ultra Stop, Auto Body Master), a proprietary electronic ordering platform called MyPlace4Parts, and warranty programs such as Confidence Plus North American Warranty and SafeRoute Roadside Assistance. The network reports approximately 3,500 certified service centers in the United States and Canada, supported by financing options and technical training for members.

Primary customers are independent automotive repair shops, parts retailers, and warehouse distributors within the automotive aftermarket. The alliance also serves fleet operators and DIY consumers through its retail locations. Member distributors such as Auto-Wares, Hahn Automotive Warehouse, and Superior Automotive Warehouse illustrate the wholesale tier, while certified service centers like Highway 7 Service Center (Iowa) and Ste-Agathe Service Centre (Manitoba) represent the retail-repair tier.

The organization emphasizes service differentiation — encapsulated in the tagline "SERVICE is the difference. We get it!" — and positions itself as a partner that provides tools, training, marketing support, and a collective voice for independents in the aftermarket. Its warranty coverage is honored across all network locations, and the ordering platform is designed to reduce administrative burden for repair shops.

name: Agave Semiconductor
old_description: Agave's Smart-Drive technology optimizes a motor's energy efficiency in real time while maintaining motor speed
about:
Agave Semiconductor is a Phoenix, Arizona-based semiconductor company focused on motor control integrated circuits. The company was founded to address energy efficiency in electric motors, though its exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. Its founder has been featured in local business media discussing the Arizona startup ecosystem.

The company designs and supplies Smart-Drive pre-driver ICs for brushless DC fans, offering both open-loop (AGV8011, AGV8012, AGV8018, AGV8019) and closed-loop (AGV8001, AGV8002, AGV8008, AGV8009) product families. These devices implement real-time efficiency optimization algorithms that adjust power delivery to maintain mechanical workload while minimizing electrical input. The AGV8009 closed-loop pre-driver, for example, provides 40 V MOS output pre-drivers capable of sourcing or sinking 100 mA, along with soft-start, current-limit, locked-rotor, and thermal protections.

Primary markets include data-center cooling, where the technology reduces electricity consumed by fans and blowers in server enclosures, as well as broader electronics cooling applications. The company's literature highlights computer server enclosures as a key environment where the pressure-airflow (PQ) curve intersection determines operating points.

Agave states that its Smart-Drive technology can achieve energy savings of up to 80 percent depending on fan pressure and airflow conditions, while also reducing motor vibration. The differentiation rests on continuous, real-time efficiency optimization that adapts to changing system impedance without sacrificing speed or workload.

about:
Agri-Industrial Plastics Co. was founded in 1978 by Dick Smith in Fairfield, Iowa. The company began by collaborating with industry leaders to advance plastic blow molding technology. After 37 years at the helm, Smith stepped down as president in 2015 and his daughter, Lori, assumed leadership, keeping the business family-owned.

The company operates a 340,000-square-foot manufacturing facility housing 20 monolayer accumulator-head blow molding machines and eight multilayer continuous coextrusion machines dedicated to producing EPA-compliant, non-automotive fuel tanks. In addition to blow molding, Agri-Industrial provides engineering and design support, assembly, packaging, and quality inspection using a Shape Grabber laser scanner for dimensional verification.

Its customer base spans the turf equipment, power sports, agricultural, and marine sectors, with additional work in lawn and garden and recreational watercraft. Long-standing clients include EXCEL Industries (Hustler Turf Equipment), Kubota Manufacturing of America, and John Deere, all of whom cite the company’s on-time delivery and design collaboration.

Agri-Industrial’s stated vision is to be the provider of innovative, high-quality blow molded solutions. The company emphasizes a systematic quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, advanced product quality planning, and Level III PPAP capability as core differentiators.

name: Air Metal VA
old_description: Founded in 1970, Air Metal has been serving the Central Virginia region with high quality custom sheet metal & roofing work for over 50 years.
about:
Air Metal VA was founded in 1970 by Douglas and Gladys Smith in Richmond, Virginia. The company has served the Central Virginia region for over five decades with custom sheet metal fabrication and metal roofing. Since 2021, the business has continued the Smiths' legacy, operating as a family-owned shop with a team that brings more than 60 years of combined fabrication experience.

The company runs a full-service fabrication shop capable of handling projects of any size. Its core work includes standing seam roofing panels — snap lock, mechanical lock, and nail strip — as well as 5V crimp roofing, metal soffit and wall panels, fascia, valleys, coping, and drip edge. Air Metal also produces custom gutters, roofing soffits, chimney caps, cupolas, conductor heads, vents, and HVAC components such as ducting, fittings, plenums, diffuser boxes, and register boxes. Historic duplication of architectural metalwork is another specialty.

Air Metal serves residential and commercial construction customers across Central Virginia, supplying roofing contractors, HVAC installers, and general contractors who need custom sheet metal components. The shop's output ranges from standard roofing panels to one-off architectural pieces for historic restoration projects.

The company emphasizes its deep regional experience and the ability to match Virginia's unpredictable weather with durable, custom-fabricated metal solutions. Its differentiator is the combination of a fully equipped fabrication shop and a team with decades of hands-on expertise, allowing it to turn nearly any project vision into reality.

name: AirFinder
old_description: Link Labs specializes in scalable, end-to-end asset visibility for manufacturing and logistics operations. Our comprehensive platform seamlessly integrates indoor and outdoor tracking to account for asset visibility needs across industries. We work with businesses of all scopes and sizes to find a solution that works for their unique challenges.
about:
Link Labs is headquartered in Annapolis, Maryland. The company was founded in 2014 by a group of veteran engineers from the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, who had previously collaborated on projects for the U.S. Department of Defense, telecommunications firms, and the intelligence community. The business remains privately held.

The company develops the AirFinder platform, an end-to-end IoT asset visibility system that combines Bluetooth Low Energy, phase ranging, and other location technologies to track assets indoors and outdoors with up to 30-centimeter accuracy. The hardware lineup includes location beacons, asset tags, access points, and gateways, all managed through a cloud-based interface. Link Labs reports processing more than two billion location, condition, and behavior events per month and holds 29 U.S. patents plus additional international patents.

AirFinder serves manufacturing operations, logistics operations, healthcare facilities, and election agencies. Customers use the system to monitor work-in-process inventory, equipment, tools, packages, and personnel in warehouses; track trailers and assets across geographies; ensure compliance for temperature-sensitive shipments; and maintain chain-of-custody for election equipment. Partnerships with Geotab and the Hubble Network extend the platform into telematics and global satellite-based tracking.

The founders built AirFinder to break the cost-performance compromise in asset tracking, aiming to deliver an affordable, scalable solution that integrates multiple location technologies without requiring expensive infrastructure. The company emphasizes low total cost of ownership, from tags and infrastructure to installation and maintenance, and highlights its ability to integrate with existing enterprise systems via MQTT and API.

name: Aire Plastics
old_description: Welcome to Aire Plastics, a family owned and operated company dedicated to serving people like you since 1989.
about:
Aire Plastics is headquartered in La Vernia, Texas, and has been family-owned since its founding in 1989. The business traces its roots to 1982 when mold maker Ken Simms established Aire Masters of San Antonio. After Simms' sudden death in 1989, Terry Post—who owned an automotive repair business on family property in Adkins, Texas—purchased the plastics division and converted his garage into a production plant. Despite having no prior injection molding experience, Post applied his background in high-precision boiler work to deliver on-time parts to the company's original six customers.

Today Aire Plastics operates a highly automated facility with nine injection molding machines ranging from 33 to 275 tons of press capacity. The shop offers rapid tooling, prototyping, 3D modeling, and proof-of-concept development alongside production services such as insert molding and over-molding. Secondary operations include ultrasonic welding, clam-shell packaging, custom packaging design, and direct-to-distribution shipping. The company employs 14 people and handles low- to high-volume runs.

The company serves its original six long-term customers while also working with inventors and product developers seeking plastics manufacturing solutions. Its customer base spans the plastics industry and includes clients needing product design, tool creation, assembly, and packaging services.

Aire Plastics emphasizes protecting intellectual property through NDAs and building long-term service records. The business was started to preserve the plastics division after its founder's death, and it differentiates itself through on-time delivery, family ownership, and a commitment to projects of any size.

Airlite Plastics Co. operates from Omaha, Nebraska, as a family-owned packaging manufacturer. The company emphasizes its long history while focusing on future-oriented innovation, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

Decoration capabilities encompass in-mold labeling, flexographic printing with up to eight colors, and dry offset printing with in-house plate production. Engineering services, custom graphics, package design, and marketing support round out the offering.

Airlite serves brands in cultured dairy, household products, horticulture, and temperature-controlled shipping, providing packaging that withstands HPP and cold-chain requirements. Customers range from food processors needing oxygen-barrier containers to horticultural suppliers and consumer-goods companies seeking custom-decorated cups and lids.

The company cites its family-owned structure as a source of responsiveness, avoiding bureaucratic layers to maintain decades-long partnerships. It highlights a track record of pioneering IML packaging, oxygen-barrier technology, and HPP-compatible containers, alongside a sustainability ethos that aims to benefit both the planet and the customer's bottom line.

name: Akrivis Components and Tools
old_description: We supply hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming equipment, wire bonders, DI water systems, and other SMT manufacturing tools.
about:
Akrivis Components and Tools is based in Henderson, Nevada, and was established in 2023. The company was created to provide North American technical sales and support for specialized electronics manufacturing equipment, bridging the gap between overseas equipment builders and domestic manufacturers who need clearer communication, application review, installation, training, and service coordination.

The company does not manufacture equipment itself but acts as a specialized process-equipment distributor and application resource. It supplies hydro-cleaning systems, vapor degreasers, lead forming equipment, wire bonders, DI water systems, and other SMT manufacturing tools. Its focus categories include cleaning and contamination control, vapor degreasing, PCB/SMT cleaning, lead forming and cutting, lead reconditioning, component tinning, wire bonding, thermal/vacuum heating, and semiconductor packaging support. Akrivis provides installation, training, service, quote coordination, and application review from a Los Angeles-area support point, covering the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

about:
The Alabama Cable & Broadband Association (ACBA) is headquartered in Montgomery, Alabama, and was founded in 1965. It operates as a trade association representing cable providers, operators, suppliers, and programmers across the state. The organization was established to give the cable industry a unified voice in legislative, regulatory, and taxation matters at the state level.

ACBA does not manufacture physical products. Instead, it provides advocacy, policy representation, and industry coordination for its member companies. Its activities include lobbying, regulatory monitoring, public affairs, and facilitating industry collaboration on broadband deployment and technology issues. The association’s staff works from its Montgomery office to engage with lawmakers, state agencies, and other stakeholders.

The association serves the cable and broadband telecommunications industry in Alabama. Its members include cable system operators, programmers, equipment suppliers, and related service providers. ACBA’s advocacy covers issues such as broadband expansion, spectrum policy, taxation, and regulatory reform that affect the cable sector statewide. The organization also highlights the industry’s economic contributions, citing more than 3,000 jobs and a $3.56 billion economic impact across Alabama.

ACBA was started to ensure the cable industry remained competitive amid rapid changes in technology, information, and communication services. Its stated purpose is to provide members with a unified voice throughout the legislative process and to support the industry’s role in education, economic development, and quality of life in Alabama.

about:
Alcan Electric & Engineering, Inc. was founded in 1971 in Anchorage, Alaska. The company is Alaskan-owned and operated, and has grown from a traditional electrical contractor into a full-service electrical, communications, security, and audio-visual technology integrator. It now employs over 200 professionals across offices in Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Wasilla, serving the entire state.

The firm delivers commercial electrical construction services including power distribution, lighting, backup power, high-voltage, and design & engineering. It also integrates low-voltage systems such as building automation, IP video surveillance (as Alaska's Milestone video pioneer), access control, structured cabling (BICSI-certified copper and fiber, and the state's only Corning preferred installer), unified communications, and audio-visual solutions. Additional offerings include turn-key commercial solar, EV charging infrastructure, and electrical maintenance programs aligned with the 2023 NFPA 70B standard. With a workforce of more than 200 and three regional offices, Alcan handles large, complex projects across Alaska.

Alcan serves healthcare, aviation, corrections, defense, and North Slope industrial clients statewide. Notable projects include a 15-year partnership with Providence Alaska Medical Center in Anchorage encompassing the 82,000-square-foot Tower M, electrical work for the 16-bay F-35 hangars at Eielson Air Force Base, and advanced controls for the Anchorage Fish Hatchery. The company also works with commercial and energy-efficient lighting projects across the state.

The company emphasizes its Alaskan ownership and deep local knowledge of conditions, codes, and logistics as a key differentiator. It highlights the scale of its workforce and its NECA and IBEW Local 1547 affiliations, which provide trained, certified craftspeople and a deep labor pool. Alcan also promotes its integrated approach — combining electrical and low-voltage technology under one roof — and a formal safety program called "Safety Zone" that goes beyond compliance with weekly project-specific safety meetings.

about:
Allied Body Works Inc. was founded in 1949 in Seattle, Washington, when Charles Walter Bull and two partners each invested $200 to leave Heiser Body and open a small garage on Fourth Avenue. The business has remained family-owned through four generations, passing from Bull to his son Owen and son-in-law Dick Minice, then to Richard Minice in 1996, and most recently to great-grandson Adam Keane, who purchased the company in February 2023 and serves as president. Headquarters is at 625 South 96th Street in Seattle’s industrial corridor.

The company operates as a full-line truck equipment distributor and upfitter, providing custom fabrication, installation, and repair for light- to medium-duty vehicles. Its shop builds service bodies, dump bodies, platform bodies, flatbeds, contractor bodies, and van bodies, and integrates cranes, liftgates, electrical and lighting accessories, and EV power systems. Allied also offers cargo van interiors, truck side guards (marketed as the Walker Blocker), and a ready-now inventory program through a partnership with Work Truck Solutions.

Customers span tradespeople, commercial fleets, government agencies, construction firms, shipping and distribution companies, and utilities across the Pacific Northwest. Early work included armored cars for Loomis; recent projects include ladder racks, shelving, and door locks for fleet vans (as noted by fleet manager Robert Salamone) and side-guard safety systems for municipal trucks. A dedicated government and fleet account team handles public-sector contracts.

The company emphasizes its family-owned culture as a differentiator, citing a standard of excellence that carries into every build. It highlights quick turnaround to meet deadlines, the ability to execute complex custom plans, and a future-focused mindset that includes safety innovations like the Walker Blocker and green options such as solar integration. The stated mission is to listen to each customer and design a solution that fits their specific operational needs.

The company distributes a comprehensive inventory of home medical equipment and supplies, including incontinence products, mobility devices, power mobility devices, and bathroom safety durable medical equipment (DME). Amador Medical maintains most items in stock and offers immediate delivery, with same-day service available for local customers.

Its customer base includes individuals with temporary or ongoing medical conditions, caregivers, and community partners throughout Southern Nevada and Idaho. The company emphasizes personalized attention and compassionate support, aiming to enable clients to receive care outside of hospital environments.

Amador Medical states that compassion is its company motto and that carrying high-quality products at affordable prices builds trust within the communities it serves. The business was started to meet budget needs and guarantee satisfaction for those requiring medical supplies and equipment.

Ambix Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 2001 in Albany, New Hampshire. The company operates as a full-service provider of custom plastic injection molding, offering design, mold building, prototyping, and contract manufacturing.

Ambix delivers end-to-end plastics manufacturing, from material selection and mold design through prototyping, process development, and high-volume production. The shop runs high-temperature molding and precision machining, and provides value-added services such as small-parts packing, sorting, and bagging in bulk or retail configurations. The company has produced millions of parts across numerous mold designs, though specific facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Ambix serves customers facing supply-chain risk, quality issues, budget constraints, and demand surges. Case studies reference clients who on-shored production to the New Hampshire plant, reduced mold costs through interchangeable components, and secured raw materials during extended lead-time periods. The company emphasizes fast turnaround on prototypes, molds, and production runs, with a focus on first-time quality and ISO 9000:2015 certification. Ambix differentiates itself through process optimization, failure analysis, automation integration, and a strong vendor network that enables domestic manufacturing and cost reduction.

Engineering support covers design for manufacturability, design assistance, material analysis and testing, tooling development, and CAD services, backed by a global procurement strategy aimed at on-time delivery.

name: American Cable Products LLC
old_description: Delivering excellence in communication connectivity since 2002
about:
American Cable Products, LLC was established in November 2002 in Lake St Louis, Missouri. The minority-owned business (MBE certified) began as a provider of low‑voltage communication connectivity solutions, aiming to serve organizations across the United States, Canada, Mexico, and U.S. territories.

The company delivers end‑to‑end infrastructure services divided into inside‑plant and outside‑plant work. Inside‑plant capabilities include structured premise cabling (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6a, and fiber), data‑center design and implementation, hardware configuration, and network infrastructure. Outside‑plant services cover provider connection points, fiber‑optic installations, campus connectivity, and inter‑building links. A security and surveillance division installs IP camera systems, access‑control and biometric solutions, with project experience exceeding 2,800 cameras. The firm also provides wireless networks, VoIP, audio‑visual, SCADA/industrial IoT, satellite communications, consulting, and ongoing maintenance. Operations span all 50 states, with regional offices supporting a project portfolio that includes 500‑plus facilities and 1,000‑plus sites.

Clients range from Fortune 500 enterprises to critical‑infrastructure operators in sectors such as data centers, healthcare, corrections, education, airports, government, retail, and manufacturing. Named references include St. Louis Lambert International Airport, a multi‑site healthcare network, a university system, a retail distribution chain, and an industrial manufacturing complex.

American Cable Products states its mission is to be a one‑stop shop for communication connectivity from the provider demarcation point to the client data center, delivering practical, high‑quality, and cost‑effective IT installation and service while exceeding customer expectations. Core values cited are quality, reliability, customer focus, and cost effectiveness.

name: American Circuits
old_description: American Circuits is an electronic contract manufacturer headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, providing turnkey printed circuit board assembly across two Charlotte facilities.
about:
American Circuits operates from Charlotte, North Carolina, where it has maintained a family-run, minority-owned contract manufacturing business for over 30 years. The company was founded by Vic Gondha, a first-generation immigrant who built the firm after arriving in the United States with a goal of owning a business. His son, Ket Gondha, now serves as CEO, having expanded the campus to two facilities totaling roughly 40,000 square feet.

The company provides turnkey printed circuit board assembly from bare-board fabrication through final box-build integration. Its services span SMT, through-hole, and mixed-technology assembly, rapid prototyping, conformal coating and potting, automated optical inspection, PCB design and reverse engineering, design-for-manufacturability analysis, BOM optimization, custom wire-harness and cable assembly, and full electro-mechanical integration. Production runs range from single prototypes to volumes exceeding 100,000 units.

American Circuits serves approximately 400 customers across defense, healthcare, robotics, and LED-lighting sectors. Named clients include TE Connectivity, Honda, and Assa Abloy, the latter a Charlotte-based security and access-control manufacturer.

The firm distinguishes itself by controlling the entire process from bare-board supply to finished assembly, a combination it says few competitors offer. It emphasizes U.S.-based manufacturing, engineering support at every stage, flexible production runs, and rapid turnarounds. The operation is ISO 9001 certified, ITAR registered, UL recognized, and compliant with RoHS, REACH, and Dodd-Frank conflict-mineral requirements.

name: American Electric Components, Inc.
old_description: Manufactures and repairs electrical transformers (single/three-phase, up to 10,000 KVA)
about:
American Electric Components, Inc. was founded in 1995 in Vernon, California, as a family-owned and operated business. The company traces its roots to a multi-generational team that brings over a century of cumulative experience to the design, fabrication, and repair of electrical transformers.

Operating from a 78,400-square-foot property with a 47,000-square-foot shop, AEC maintains complete in-house control over manufacturing, from initial engineering through final testing. The facility produces and refurbishes single- and three-phase dry-type and oil-filled transformers rated up to 10,000 kVA and 69,000 volts, along with reactors, padmounts, saturable current transformers, inverter-duty units, and desalter transformers. A large stock of new, rebuilt, and repaired units is kept on hand for immediate sale or rental.

The company serves utility, industrial, commercial, and desalination customers nationwide. It is a certified repair center for both ABB and General Electric, meaning its technicians are factory-trained and its processes follow original equipment manufacturer standards. Clients range from utilities needing rapid replacement units to industrial plants requiring on-site oil leak repair, electrical testing, and preventive maintenance.

AEC emphasizes end-to-end oversight of the production cycle, adherence to NEMA, ANSI, IEEE, and UL standards, and the ability to deploy field service crews for emergency repairs. The combination of a deep inventory, certified OEM repair credentials, and a legacy of family stewardship is presented as the foundation of its reliability.

American Howa Kentucky, Inc. Georgetown Plant (AHK-GT) is located in Midway, Kentucky. The facility was established in 2017 as part of the North American expansion of HOWA USA Holdings, Inc., which traces its U.S. presence to a 2004 plant in Indiana. The plant produces automotive interior components, including headliners, sunshades, dash insulators, felt products, and polyurethane foam parts. Production capabilities include felt manufacturing, PU foam processing (with two foam lines), and on-site headliner assembly. The facility supports programs for multiple automakers, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not disclosed.

The Georgetown plant serves the automotive industry, supplying Tier 1 and OEM customers. Its client list includes Nissan North America (for the Leaf, Murano, Titan, and Frontier), Toyota Motor North America, American Honda Motor Co., Aisin World Corp. of America, and Webasto Product North America.

The company's stated mission emphasizes employee well-being, unique product development through boldness and creativity, environmental conservation, continuous improvement for customer satisfaction, and contribution to local development. The Georgetown plant was added to expand capacity for PU foam and headliner production in support of growing North American demand.

about:
American Iron Works operates from a shop in New Haven, Connecticut. The business traces its roots back over 40 years to a passion for metal craft held by Pasquale, the father and grandfather of the current owners. Today it is a third‑generation, family‑owned company led by Anthony and Joe Maresca, who have grown the operation into a full‑service fabrication and installation house serving clients across Connecticut.

The company produces custom ornamental metal fabrications in iron, stainless steel, aluminum, and bronze. Its in‑house capabilities span welding (Stick, MIG, TIG), metal forming (grinding, cutting, chamfering, bending, punching, shearing, and CNC plasma cutting), and finishing (sandblasting, powder coating, galvanizing, and patinas). Every project moves through material sourcing, fabrication, finishing, and installation under one roof, with each piece inspected before it leaves the shop.

American Iron Works serves both commercial and residential customers. Commercial projects have included fire‑escape renovations, steel mezzanines, anti‑climb fencing, and custom partition walls for office and retail spaces. Residential work ranges from hand‑forged stair rails and Juliet balconies to aluminum pergolas, cable‑rail systems, and decorative gates. The shop also fabricates specialty items such as sunburst panels, branch‑textured railings, and custom signage.

The Maresca brothers emphasize fine craftsmanship, custom design, and efficiency as the pillars of their reputation. They attribute their longevity to a hands‑on approach that controls every step from raw material to final installation, ensuring each client receives a unique, detail‑oriented piece.

American Metal Fabricators was founded in 1988 in Gastonia, North Carolina, just outside Charlotte. The company operates as a custom metal fabrication shop and has served the region for over three decades. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company fabricates a wide range of custom equipment including air washers, air handling units, foam panels, energy recovery systems, dryers, ovens, furnaces, plenums, duct systems, dust filtration equipment, gas turbine filtration, mining equipment, humidification systems, mist eliminators, acoustic enclosures, scrubbers, spray systems, and evaporative cooling systems. American Metal Fabricators serves industries such as power generation, utilities, microelectronics, paper, pulp, fibers, textiles, wood, furniture, food and beverage, chemicals, plastics, paint, printing, heavy equipment, and pharmaceuticals. Customers include utilities, industrial equipment manufacturers, and facilities requiring custom metal enclosures and filtration systems.

The company emphasizes its ability to handle complex jobs with short lead times, supported by a large skilled labor force that allows rapid expansion. It is equipped for both large-scale projects and special handling of smaller orders, with in-house capabilities spanning welding, forming, blasting, painting, rolling, assembly, and foam panel manufacturing.

American Precision Products was founded in 1972 in Huntsville, Alabama. The company operates as a custom injection molding firm serving commercial, aerospace, and government markets. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company molds thermoplastics, thermoplastic elastomers, and thermoset materials, including filled and modified resins. Its processes encompass custom injection molding, compression molding, transfer molding, insert molding, overmolding, and miniature and micro molding. Additional services include prototyping, in-house mold building and tooling, and overseas tooling sourcing. Production runs range from low volume to high volume, with micro molding capabilities on dedicated high-speed presses since 1987.

American Precision Products serves military, aerospace, and commercial industries. The firm emphasizes highly controlled manufacturing specifications—tolerances, cosmetics, and production control measures—tailored for aerospace and military applications. Customers include government agencies and commercial OEMs requiring precision molded components.

The company positions its injection molding as faster, more accurate, and more repeatable than traditional compression and transfer molding, offering a path to cost savings and quality improvements for existing programs. Its differentiators include micro molding expertise since 1987, in-house tooling, and the ability to manage both short and long production runs.

about:
American Sheet Metal Fabricators, Inc. (ASM) operates a Union Local 73 fabrication shop in South Holland, Illinois, on Chicago’s south side. The business is led by members of the DeBartolo family: Dennis DeBartolo serves as president, Frank DeBartolo as vice president, Anthony DeBartolo as superintendent, and Christine DeBartolo as treasurer. The company does not disclose its founding year.

ASM produces HVAC ductwork and fittings in a variety of configurations. Its capabilities include lockforming rectangular straight duct and fittings, snaplock and Pittsburgh lock fabrication, welded construction of rectangular and round duct (with TIG welding available), double-wall rectangular and spiral duct with solid or perforated inner liners, and spiral pipe from 4 to 40 inches in diameter. The shop also installs acoustical liner (Armaflex, Armacell), fabricates roof caps, custom drain pans, roof curbs, platform curbs, and roof rails, and supplies accessories such as canvas, Ductmate frames, TDF hardware, sealers, and screws. Additional services include end wrapping, custom register and linear boxes, painted pipe chase covers, painted duct, pre-assembled duct runs with collars and taps installed, and cut-to-size cleats and drives. All work is fabricated to SMACNA standards.

The company serves mechanical and HVAC contractors, with testimonials referencing customers such as EMCOR Team. Its product line covers commercial and residential applications, including roof-top units, residential plenums, and return-air elbows available for same-day pick-up.

ASM emphasizes a customer-driven approach, offering high-quality products at reasonable prices. Differentiators include a large inventory of low-pressure snaplock pipe and fittings, same-day pick-up for select items, and pre-assembled duct runs delivered sealed and ready to install.

name: American Wood Design, Inc.
old_description: Award-Winning Commercial Cabinetry & Architectural Millwork Since 1996
about:
American Wood Design, Inc. is a family-owned commercial cabinetry and architectural millwork shop based in Chester, Pennsylvania. The company was founded in 1996 by Michael Gilhool Sr., who launched the business above a doctor's office in South Philadelphia after his previous employer closed its display shop. Gilhool bartered the shop's machinery for cabinetry work, and the operation later spent nearly two decades at Naamans Road Business Park before moving to a 16,000-square-foot facility in Chester in 2017.

The shop produces custom cabinets, countertops, reception desks, nurse stations, and a full range of architectural millwork including office front systems, wall paneling, and custom trim. Its equipment includes a computerized beam saw, CNC router, and edgebander driven by dedicated software, allowing both high-volume production runs and the flexibility to handle small projects. Services also cover plastic laminate layups with a 3–5 day turnaround, solid surface and stone countertop fabrication, and ongoing maintenance and repair work.

The company serves commercial contractors, architects, and facility managers across the Greater Philadelphia region. Typical projects span office fit-outs, healthcare environments, and retail spaces, with concrete examples including custom reception desks for corporate lobbies, nurse stations for medical facilities, and wholesale plastic laminate panel layups for trade customers.

The founding mission — to build cabinetry and relationships that last a lifetime — emphasizes on-time, on-budget craftsmanship. Gilhool's original impetus was turning a layoff into an opportunity, and the business continues to stress quick turnaround, competitive pricing on wholesale press jobs, and a willingness to handle service calls and modifications long after installation.

about:
Amphenol DC Electronics operates from a 70,000-square-foot facility in San Jose, California, with additional manufacturing sites in Nogales, Mexico, and Malaysia. The company was founded in 1979 by David Cianciulli after he left Hughes Aircraft to start a cable sales and distribution business. Within a few years, the operation added engineers and assemblers to produce custom cable and wire harness solutions for technical instrument manufacturers. In 2013, the business was acquired by Amphenol Corporation, becoming a division known as Amphenol DC Electronics (ADCE).

ADCE specializes in the design, engineering, and manufacture of custom wire harnesses, cable assemblies, and integrated electronic mechanical devices (box builds). The company handles both high- and low-volume production runs, offering build-to-print services, prototyping, and custom tooling design.

about:
Amsted Automotive is headquartered in Saginaw, Michigan. The company traces its roots to 1903 with the founding of Burgess-Norton. The current entity was formed in 2021 through the integration of Burgess-Norton (established 1903) and Means Industries (established 1922), along with Transform Automotive (1997) and SMW Manufacturing (2004). No ownership tags are disclosed.

Amsted Automotive designs and manufactures high-performance components for vehicle and industrial applications. Its product portfolio includes brackets and welded assemblies, residential and industrial coupler components, piston pins and bearing products, forestry, trenching and wear parts, and powertrain components. The company employs over 2,000 people worldwide and operates 21 manufacturing facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia, including 13 in the United States. Annual production exceeds 200 million components. Core manufacturing processes encompass advanced metal forming (flow forming, in-die spline forming, grob forming, laser welding, stamping), cold forming and finishing, powder metallurgy, and propulsion systems such as torque management and clutch technologies.

The company serves global automotive, off-highway, mining, and industrial markets. Its components are used in internal combustion, hybrid, and electric powertrains for passenger cars, heavy-duty trucks, and off-highway equipment. Customers include automakers and industrial OEMs seeking net-shape metal components and complex assemblies.

Amsted Automotive emphasizes its global footprint as a differentiator, stating that its 13 U.S.-based facilities minimize tariff risks and supply delays by enabling regional manufacturing. The company also highlights its century-long manufacturing legacy and integrated capabilities spanning metal forming, powder metallurgy, and propulsion solutions as key to delivering high-quality, cost-effective components.

old_description: Andy Sanchez and his sons are celebrated furniture artists, renowned for their craftsmanship in the creation of remarkable live edge furniture adorned with beautiful stones and gems. Their distinctive pieces honor the inherent beauty of wood, maintaining its natural contours to integrate an outdoor essence indoors. Every piece is a work of art, meticulously shaped from fine woods like black walnut, alligator juniper, and eucalyptus and many other exotic woods. about:
Andy Sanchez Furniture operates from Algodones, New Mexico, where Andy Sanchez and his sons Aaron and Daniel have been crafting original furniture for nearly three decades. The family-owned workshop, run by Andy and his wife Cheryl alongside their seven children, began with a commitment to creating heirloom pieces that honor the natural character of wood.

The shop specializes in live-edge furniture that incorporates precious stones, gems, and metals into slabs of black walnut, alligator juniper, eucalyptus, and other exotic species. Rather than imposing a design on the material, the artisans let each log’s grain and form dictate the piece, often employing book-matched cuts sourced from dead-standing trees in the Gila National Forest. Every project is a one-off collaboration: clients exchange photos and measurements with the makers to refine dimensions, stone placement, and overall composition until the piece matches the client’s vision.

The clientele consists primarily of residential customers seeking custom tables, chairs, and statement pieces for their homes. Testimonials cite buyers from Pennsylvania and features in New Mexico Magazine, underscoring a reach beyond the local area. The firm does not serve commercial or industrial markets; its output is limited to bespoke, art-grade furnishings.

The founders’ guiding principle is to work with nature rather than alter it. As Andy Sanchez puts it, the intention is not to change what has been created but to appreciate what is already provided. This philosophy drives the use of fully cured, dead-standing timber and the practice of pairing wood with stones from the same locale, aiming to produce furniture that gains value and sentiment across generations.

Apocalypse Design Inc. has been designing and manufacturing rugged outdoor gear in Fairbanks, Alaska, since 1983. The company was founded by Dick Flaharty, who named the business after the Apocalypse, a 9,000-foot peak in the remote Revelation Mountains that caught his eye during a winter expedition. Today, the family-owned operation is led by Flaharty's son Tyson and his wife Davya, both lifelong Alaskans who grew up in Fairbanks and bring extensive endurance-sport experience to the brand.

Every garment and piece of equipment—from expedition parkas and wind anoraks to fleece layers, duffle bags, and backpacks—is designed and sewn at the company's Fairbanks facility on Minnie Street. The shop focuses on custom manufacturing, meticulous material selection, and innovative pattern work tailored for arctic conditions. All products carry a lifetime warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.

The gear is used worldwide by outdoor adventurers, polar explorers, climbers, dog mushers, skiers, snowmachiners, hikers, cyclists, paddlers, scientists, filmmakers, pilots, and hunters who require reliable protection in extreme cold. The customer base spans professional guides, research teams, and discerning consumers seeking made-in-Alaska quality.

The company's founding ethos centers on protection, ingenuity, understanding, endurance, and performance—values shaped by the founders' own adventures on Alaska's trails and mountains. By keeping design and production under one roof, Apocalypse Design maintains direct control over every stitch, ensuring that each item meets the demands of the environments that inspired its name.

Arcamed is based in Indianapolis, Indiana. The company was founded in 2012 by Greg Maurer and Kevin Etzkorn after they recognized that orthopedic original equipment manufacturers were consistently underserved by their supply chain, facing long lead times, poor quality control, and weak customer service.

Arcamed manufactures surgical case and tray systems, precision caddies for implants, and rigid sterilization containers. The facility operates under 5S and Lean Manufacturing principles and is equipped with an automated optical assembly inspection system, a coordinate measuring machine (CMM), a Micro‑Vu vision system, and an optical comparator. The company reports quality metrics including 99.1 % on‑time delivery, 96.9 % on‑time‑in‑full, and 98.4 % orders defect‑free.

The customer base spans enterprise, mid‑market, and startup orthopedic OEMs. Arcamed positions itself as an extension of its partners’ teams, providing design transfer support, validated processes, and documentation that meets regulatory requirements.

The founders started Arcamed to deliver concierge‑level service, industry‑lead times, and on‑time delivery — commitments the company says differentiate it from transactional suppliers. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 13485:2016 and the facility is FDA registered.

about:
Archbold Furniture has operated in Archbold, Ohio since 1900. The company is led by owner and president Pat McNamara and now encompasses three brands: Archbold Furniture, Amish Essentials, and Bob Timberlake® American Home.

The company manufactures solid wood furniture for every room — bedroom, dining, living room, home office, bookcases, and kitchen storage. Production uses select solid hardwoods such as alder and maple, with English dovetail drawer construction and smooth glides. Finishes are applied by Amish craftsmen using catalyzed conversion varnish for moisture, heat, and scratch resistance. The firm maintains a showroom in High Point, North Carolina, and sells through a dealer network.

Archbold Furniture serves the residential furniture market, supplying dealers who sell to end consumers. Its three brands address different price points and styles: the core Archbold line features solid alder with custom Amish finishes; Amish Essentials offers 100% Amish-handcrafted pieces from locally sourced hardwoods; and Bob Timberlake® American Home presents artist-designed collections built by American craftsmen.

The company cites its Christian values and a commitment to “quality furniture, backed by extraordinary service at a value to our customers” as guiding principles. Pat McNamara emphasizes continual improvement to ensure a satisfied customer for life. Differentiators include American-made construction since 1900, solid tops and sides, and a finish system designed for durability.

Customers span automotive repair shops, commercial garages, fleet maintenance operations, and personal garage owners throughout the Southwest. The company's inspectors are qualified to examine any lift regardless of manufacturer, brand, or age, issuing serialized ALI inspection labels that serve as proof of compliance for code enforcement.

The Byerses emphasize a personal-touch approach, offering personalized service, a comprehensive catalog, and a 100% satisfaction guarantee. Their ALI-certified inspectors and focus on OSHA compliance differentiate the business in a market where safety certification is often a minimum requirement.

The company provides electronic manufacturing services including surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, component sourcing, prototyping, and functional testing. Its capabilities span from hand placement of leaded components to automated machine placement of fine-pitch parts and BGAs, accommodating board sizes from small to large with mixed through-hole and single- or double-sided SMT. Additional services include in-circuit testing, full unit build, and cable and harness assembly. Quality processes feature automated optical inspection (AOI) on all boards after reflow, with optical character recognition on SMT components, and inspection to IPC-A-610 Class II (Class III available).

Aspen Electronics serves customers in the defense sector, evidenced by its ITAR registration with the U.S. Department of Defense, as well as broader electronics manufacturers requiring PCB assembly and test. Clients engage directly with an engineering-background manager from the first interaction, eliminating internal translation of technical requirements.

The company emphasizes lean manufacturing integrated throughout production, targeting a defect rate near zero through thorough functional testing. It promotes fair pricing supported by supplier relationships and commits to on-time delivery, with staff often working overtime to meet deadlines.

name: Assembled Products, Inc.
old_description: Specializing in Prototypes, Small to Medium Production Electronics Assembly  and Manufacutring since 1986
about:
Assembled Products, Inc. was founded in 1986 by Michael Stevens in Collierville, Tennessee, before relocating to Piperton, Tennessee in 1990 and later to a 33,000‑square‑foot facility in the Elgin community near Rogersville, Alabama. The company is woman‑owned and operates as a small business with approximately ten employees.

The shop provides printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) using surface‑mount, through‑hole, and mixed‑technology processes, along with electromechanical box builds, wire‑harness fabrication, conformal coating, and functional testing. In‑house capabilities extend to design‑for‑manufacturability review, repair and rework, 3D printing, CAD drawing, patent research, and new‑product consulting. The facility also houses machining, plastic molding, and urethane/resin casting equipment to support complete product development from prototype through low‑to‑medium‑volume production.

Customers span military electronics upgrades, custom electronics, and general industrial electronics. Named accounts have included Federal Express, AutoZone, the University of Memphis, Hypertech, and IBS, alongside individual inventors and hobbyists. The company serves the southeastern United States — Alabama, Tennessee, Mississippi, Georgia, and Florida — as well as national clients.

Assembled Products positions itself on quality over low‑cost offshore alternatives, emphasizing quick response times, transparent communication, and U.S.‑based manufacturing leveraging Alabama’s low labor and tax rates. The founder started the business after his previous employer declined small jobs, a focus that remains central to the operation.

about:
Assemblies Unlimited, Inc. was founded in 1993 by Randy Shaw in Bloomingdale, Illinois. Shaw, a Northern Illinois University graduate with a background in industrial packaging sales at firms like Illinois Tool Works and Molex, started the company to build a national network of contract packaging vendors (co-packers) for food and non-food applications. The privately held company maintains its corporate headquarters in Bloomingdale with regional sales offices in Irvine, California, and Garden City, New York.

The company provides turnkey contract packaging and fulfillment services across more than 20 plant locations nationwide. Capabilities span primary and secondary packaging for both food and non-food products, including liquid and dry filling (bottles, pouches, VFFS, HFFS), hand assembly, bindery, repackaging, labeling, blister packaging, bundling, shrink wrapping, kitting, and clean-room operations. Several facilities are certified to 21 CFR Part 111 for pharmaceutical (RX/OTC) packaging and to SQF Level 3 for food safety. The Reno, Nevada site alone offers over 300,000 square feet of warehousing. Typical production runs start at a minimum of 25,000 units per SKU.

Assemblies Unlimited serves a broad range of industries: food and beverage (snacks, confectionery, nuts, gummies, protein powders, seasonings), pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals (RX/OTC drugs, supplements), household and automotive chemicals (adhesives, car care), and general retail. Customers range from large consumer packaged goods (CPG) corporations to emerging startups launching their first product.

The firm emphasizes three differentiators: quick turnaround through streamlined processes, seamless project management that covers sourcing, inventory control, and logistics, and a responsive customer experience backed by three decades of hands-on expertise across thousands of retail packaging projects.

about:
Astro Sheet Metal Co., Inc. is a family-owned custom metal fabrication company founded in 1967 in Irving, Texas. Now headquartered in Grand Prairie, Texas, the company has operated for over five decades under family ownership.

The shop provides architectural and industrial metal solutions, handling projects from design assistance and submittal drawings through mockup fabrication, brake forming of metal up to 14 feet long, welding, cutting, and final installation. It serves general contractors and subcontractors with architectural metal scopes for bar areas, ceilings, elevator entries, and reception areas, while also supplying custom fittings, hoppers, platforms, and transitions for food-service and plant-maintenance clients. Rush delivery is offered throughout the Dallas/Fort Worth and Austin regions.

Astro's project portfolio spans healthcare (OU Medical Center, Texas Health Resources), hospitality (Bowie House Hotel, Hall Park Hotel), entertainment (Meow Wolf), education (College Station City Hall), government, commercial real estate (AMLI Fountain Place, Granite Park), and retail (Crocs Storefront). Its customers include designers, builders, general contractors, and subcontractors across Texas and Oklahoma.

The company emphasizes rapid turnaround times and a single-source approach from consulting to installation, a model shaped by its founding focus on precision and speed. Family ownership and over 50 years of experience are cited as foundations for its reliability in delivering complex architectural metalwork on schedule.

name: Atlas Precision Inc
old_description: Since 1979, Atlas Precision Plastics has been committed to providing high-quality, cost-effective, plastic injection molding
about:
Atlas Precision Inc. traces its roots to April 1979, when Johann W. Hofschuster founded Atlas Mold Inc. in Arden, North Carolina, to design and build injection molds. In 1988 the company added a custom molding division, Atlas Precision Plastics, and installed its first molding machines the following year. The two operations were combined under one roof in 2006, and the business has remained under Hofschuster's leadership as president and chief executive.

Today the firm operates as a full-service injection molder with 33 presses ranging from 80 to 360 tons, each equipped with a robot or sprue picker. The production floor runs 24/7 across four crews, supported by an on-site toolroom that designs, builds, and maintains multi-cavity tooling, including core-pull, unscrewing, overmolding, and hot-runner systems. A quality lab and RJG/eDart process monitoring complement the molding operation, while 3D printing provides prototype parts. The company works with engineered resins and wood-composite materials.

Atlas serves the healthcare, automotive, telecommunications, industrial, and electrical markets, producing components for medical devices, electrical connectors, packaging, and single-use consumer products. Long-standing customers include Johnson & Johnson (Personal Care and Vistakon divisions), S.C. Johnson, Bic Corporation, Robert Bosch Automotive, Tyco Electronics, and Trex.

The company emphasizes a one-stop-shop model, assigning each customer a dedicated account manager who coordinates design, tooling, molding, and packaging. Hofschuster's team highlights its reputation for building fast-cycling, low-maintenance tooling and holds ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, CSA International, and UL certifications.

about:
Auto Recyclers operates from a 30-acre site on the I-80 service road in Rock Springs, Wyoming. The business was founded in 1980 and has been owned and operated by the Liggett family since its inception. What began as a local salvage yard has grown into a multi-acre operation with a national shipping footprint.

The company maintains an inventory of over 100,000 parts across roughly 2,800 vehicles, supplying used and new auto components to customers across the country. In addition to parts sales, Auto Recyclers runs an in-house transmission and powertrain rebuild facility that specializes in rear-wheel-drive and truck applications, covering classic units such as the TH400, TH350, C4, C6, and modern automatics including the 4L60E, 4L80E, 68RFE, and 6L80E. The shop also rebuilds manual transmissions and transfer cases. Towing and recovery services are offered with a fleet that includes two wreckers, three flatbed tow trucks, tracked snow cats, and light UTV recovery vehicles.

Customers range from independent repair shops and ranchers in the Rock Springs area to collectors and performance builders nationwide. The company’s network of more than 4,000 partner salvage yards allows it to source parts beyond its own stock, and it also procures new old-stock and aftermarket components through dealer relationships.

The Liggett family emphasizes a reputation built on honest pricing, a proper-fit guarantee, and formal warranty terms on every part sold. Their approach is framed by 45 years of consistent service rather than marketing slogans, and they highlight the combined 50-plus years of hands-on automotive experience among their staff as a practical advantage when customers need help identifying the right component.

about:
Autokiniton’s Greenville-area operation is part of a global automotive supplier formed in May 2018 when KPS Capital Partners and George Thanopoulos created Autokiniton Global Group to acquire L&W Group, a Tier 1 specialist in metal stampings, welded assemblies and tubular products. The combined entity acquired Tower International in September 2019, creating the second-largest body-in-white and vehicle-frame supplier in North America with $2.3 billion in annual sales. The company is headquartered in Fountain Inn, South Carolina, and operates as a private-equity-backed manufacturer.

The company produces high-strength structural components and precision stamping assemblies for vehicle body-in-white and frame structures. Its manufacturing portfolio includes joining and welding (MIG, resistance spot, laser, friction stir, capacitive discharge and drawn arc), complex assemblies such as front/rear floor pans and door/pillar units, tube forming on three tube mills and two roll-form mills, cold stamping on 214 tandem presses (up to 3,000 tons), 40 transfer presses (up to 3,000 tons) and 105 progressive presses (up to 1,600 tons), hot stamping on eight lines with 23 in-die quenching lasers, and laser cutting on 40 machines. facilities, four in Mexico, one in Brazil and a technology center in India.

Autokiniton serves the automotive industry as a Tier 1 supplier to the world’s automakers — Ford recognized the company with a World Excellence Award in 2021 — and also supplies tubular products to the trailer and recreational vehicle markets. Its plants are strategically located near customer assembly sites to streamline logistics.

The company says its differentiation comes from a focus on value-driven, sustainable lightweighting solutions, proprietary expertise in joining dissimilar metals (aluminum, hot-formed and ultra-high-strength steels), extensive press and hot-stamping capacity, a global footprint co-located with OEMs, and a culture that prioritizes speed, simplification and empowered problem-solving over bureaucracy.

The company stocks and sells new and rebuilt automotive parts, supplies, paint, and accessories for domestic and imported cars, trucks, and high-performance vehicles. Its inventory spans auto motor parts, electrical components, air conditioning parts, batteries, detailing products, auto body supplies, fluids, and tools. Today, Peter Okino and his son Darin Okino manage a staff of over 35 employees, many recruited from Hawaii Community College’s auto body and repair programs, with some technicians boasting over 30 years of experience.

ASC serves retail and commercial customers across the Big Island, including DIY vehicle owners, repair shops, and fleet operators needing parts for everything from light trucks to heavy-duty 4×4s. The shop carries parts for major brands such as Honda, Ford, and Toyota, and supports both foreign and domestic models.

The Okino family attributes the company’s longevity to its knowledgeable staff and deep local ties, which enable a wide inventory selection and competitive pricing. The business was founded to meet the community’s need for reliable automotive parts and has adapted through natural disasters and growth while remaining locally based.

Avon Lake Sheet Metal Company, Inc. has been family-owned and operated since 1953 in Avon Lake, Ohio, about 25 miles west of Cleveland. The business began in a one-car garage when founders George Wightman and Carl Wetzig Sr. established the shop on principles of honesty and hard work. Second-generation owners Carl Wetzig Jr. and Gary Wightman continue to lead the company today.

The company runs a 32,000-square-foot facility on a five-acre industrial site equipped with modern machinery including a Trumpf TruLaser 2030 4,000-watt fiber laser, a Trumpf TruBend 2100 press brake, a Wysong 12-foot 175-ton hydraulic press brake, a Lockformer Vulcan 2900 dual-table CNC plasma cutter, and a Fasti FP60 CNC panel former. Field services cover equipment installation, field welding, plant maintenance, project management, and coordination drawings. The shop also provides turnkey HVAC system design, duct fabrication, and installation, plus custom machine guarding fabrication and installation.

Avon Lake Sheet Metal serves a diverse customer base across automotive, steel and foundry, chemical, plastics, construction, food processing, general manufacturing, retail, education, and health care industries. The company also works with medical groups, industrial mills, and bulk powder material handling systems.

The founders' original emphasis on honesty, hard work, and lasting value remains central. AWS-certified welders and a drug-free workplace certification further underscore its operational standards.

The company produces trailer axles, components, and accessories—including hardware kits, spring latch assemblies, and a range of nuts, bolts, and shackle straps. Production centers on CNC machining, laser cutting, metal fabrication, stamping, and custom manufacturing, allowing the shop to handle both small specialty projects and larger production runs. The facility also prepares trucks for in-state and out-of-state delivery.

Axles Plus serves the trailer industry, supplying equipment trailers, travel trailers, horse trailers, and other trailer types. Customers include individual trailer owners who visit the retail showroom for parts such as tongue hitches, trailer jacks, bearings, LED lights, and bulk tires and wheels, as well as commercial trailer builders needing custom axle assemblies.

The company emphasizes that customer service is its top goal and that quality is never optional, combining modern technology with American-made craftsmanship to deliver dependable products. It highlights its ability to adapt and invest in advanced production capabilities while maintaining the values that shaped the business.

about:
Axon Medical Technologies is based in New Cumberland, Pennsylvania. The company was founded in 2003 by Michael Zarreii, who serves as chief executive and chief scientific officer. Zarreii began the venture as a philanthropic effort to explore the connection between the brain’s involuntary sensory functions and cognition, aiming to develop advanced diagnostic and therapeutic devices.

The company designs and manufactures two primary platforms: ECAT™, a point-of-care multi-screening system for primary care clinics, and Intellig-EYES™, a neurological performance measurement headgear. Both are produced in an FDA-registered facility in the United States. The platforms automate assessments such as pupillometry, cognitive testing (Trail Making Test, GPCOG, MMSE, CAPS-5), and rapid concussion screening. Axon Medical is currently expanding its manufacturing capacity to serve both commercial and military markets.

The technology targets primary care and family practice clinics, as well as military healthcare settings. The U.S. Army has funded a four-year study to integrate ECAT and Intellig-EYES into treatment protocols for service members. The platforms also support sports medicine through sideline concussion detection. Customers include clinic owners and healthcare providers who lease the devices under a per-scan billing model with CPT code reimbursement.

Zarreii’s original vision was to solve complex neurological challenges through non-invasive, objective, and automated testing. The company differentiates itself with portable, lightweight devices that generate real-time, color-coded results and clinical documentation, all while minimizing financial risk for providers through a leasing structure rather than direct sales.

Customers include meat processors, delis, ranchers, grocers, farmers’ markets, taxidermists, industrial plants, and individual buyers throughout Montana and Wyoming. B & L Scales emphasizes hands-on, on-site support — a tradition dating to its founding — with a policy of servicing both the equipment it sells and equipment from other sources. Bally Ribbon Mills operates from Bally, Pennsylvania, where it has manufactured narrow woven fabrics since 1923. The company began as a specialist in engineered webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics, and has remained a U.S.-based producer throughout its history.

Medical clients receive Class I–III device components such as orthopedic strapping, prosthetic textiles, and dental biotextiles. Safety-market products meet UL and NFPA standards for structural, proximity, and wildland fire-fighting gear.

The company began as a partnership, transitioned to family ownership for 28 years, then to single ownership before becoming 100 % employee‑owned in its 41st year of operation. This ownership structure underpins a family‑centric culture that the firm says drives its growth and financial resilience.

The firm is a self‑performing contractor that fabricates and installs miscellaneous steel and architectural metalwork. Its services span estimating, design‑assist, 3D BIM modeling (using Tekla Structures), laser scanning, project management, and full‑scale production in over 55,000 sq ft of shop and office space across multiple buildings. Two dedicated divisions handle structural steel and high‑end architectural metals such as stainless steel, bronze, aluminum, and glass.

BAPKO works primarily for general contractors throughout California on commercial, healthcare, educational, industrial, hospitality, and sports‑entertainment projects. Notable installations include the Gaylord Pacific Resort & Convention Center in Chula Vista, the Intuit Dome (Clippers Arena) in Inglewood, and the Din Tai Fung restaurant at Downtown Disney in Anaheim.

The company emphasizes its all‑in‑one, self‑perform model as a differentiator, citing proactive project management, rapid turnaround, and the integration of emerging technologies like 3D laser scanning. Employee ownership is presented as a source of financial stability and a commitment to long‑term client relationships.

name: Bardot Plastics
old_description: Three generations of expertise delivering precision parts since 1973. Our modern facility with state-of-the-art equipment ensures quality at every step.
about:
Bardot Plastics operates from a modern facility in Easton, Pennsylvania, where it has been manufacturing precision injection-molded parts since 1973. The company was founded by J. Lee Boucher and remains a third-generation family business, now led by his sons Chris, Jim, and Rick Boucher. What began as a vision for superior injection molding has grown into a full-service operation built on the principle of “making it right the first time.”

The shop specializes in large-tonnage molding, running presses up to 1,760 tons to produce large, complex components that many molders cannot accommodate. Its end-to-end capabilities cover design consultation, integrated tooling (single-cavity, multi-cavity, and family molds), insert molding, sonic welding, sub-assembly, and in-house packaging and fulfillment. A 120-ton central chilling unit and robotic part-removal systems support consistent quality across prototype and high-volume runs, working with both engineered and non-engineered resins.

Bardot serves a diverse industrial base including office furniture, lawn and garden, waste and recycling, industrial equipment, military, construction, agricultural, and commercial markets. Customers rely on the company for ergonomic workplace components, durable industrial parts, military-spec precision pieces, weather-resistant outdoor products, structural components, and agricultural parts built to withstand harsh environments.

The company differentiates itself through continuous technology investment — exemplified by the recent chilling unit installation — and a single-point-of-contact project management model. Its guiding principles of excellence, innovation, sustainability, and partnership reflect a heritage of delivering tight tolerances and dimensional stability regardless of part size or complexity.

old_description: is the best choice for fast skilled repair work on a variety of industrial equipment.
about:
Basic E Inc. operates from Charlotte, Vermont, where it maintains a 34,000-square-foot warehouse stocked with 86,000 line items. The company's founding date and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The business functions primarily as a franchised distributor of obsolete and military-specification electronic and electrical components for electric generating utilities. It stocks passives, electro-mechanicals, actives, wire-and-cable, and MIL-SPEC parts from franchised lines such as Barker Microfarads and Capteks, all backed by certificates of compliance and full traceability. Beyond distribution, Basic E provides repair services for industrial equipment, custom cable and harness assembly to customer specifications, and an asset-recovery program that purchases surplus new inventory outright.

Its customer base includes more than 35 nuclear power plants and other electric utility operators that rely on hard-to-find replacement parts for critical infrastructure. The company also serves broader industrial markets needing electronic components, motors, valves, relays, circuit boards, and related equipment.

Basic E positions itself as a one-stop source for obsolete parts with rapid turnaround, emphasizing its franchised authorization, traceable documentation, and ability to supply both components and finished cable assemblies from a single facility.

old_description: At Bauer Fabrication & Art Metal based in Waterbury, VT, we take pride in the artistic execution of our customers’ projects. Bauer Fabrication & Art Metal operates from Waterbury, Vermont, as a metal fabricating and machine shop specializing in architectural metal work, custom furniture, and original artwork. The company serves architects, designers, contractors, and homeowners throughout New England and beyond, with installations in New York City, Boston, Florida, Mississippi, California, and the Virgin Islands.

In its Waterbury facility, the team combines traditional hand-and-eye craftsmanship with a patented thermal-spray-and-wire-mesh process branded as Bauer Art Metal. This proprietary method builds freestanding objects by spraying molten metal, enabling sculptural artwork, memorials, and household items such as sinks and cookware that would otherwise require casting. The shop also provides design services and installation, coordinating with other trades when needed.

Clients include Gossens Bachman Architects, which has commissioned complex stairways and custom sinks, and Planeta Design Group of Boston, a long-term collaborator on boundary-pushing projects. Residential customers such as Howard and Linda Awand have received one-of-a-kind garden fences. The firm works across construction, architectural, residential, and art markets, delivering custom stair rails, staircases, furniture, memorials, and decorative objects.

The company distinguishes itself by welcoming challenging, non-repetitive jobs and by integrating its patented thermal-spray technique with conventional fabrication to create unique textures and forms. Its stated intention is to deliver a finish of excellent and uniform quality on every custom piece.
